title: Encrypted links between nodes, a node in the browser, Lotus Desktop

hero.alt: Lotus Desktop mining with two GPUs

intro: Nodes now encrypt the links between them, the node's pages carry a small Lotus node that runs in the visitor's browser, and Lotus Desktop arrives: one app to mine, hold a wallet and vote with RANK.

alerts.text: **Napoleon, 2026-12-21 20:50 UTC:** every node must run 12.5.1 or later before then. This version qualifies. Earlier versions, 12.4.x included, do not follow the chain after the fork.

items.lead: A Lotus node in the browser.
items.text: The node's pages turn the visitor's browser into a small Lotus node that checks block headers itself. The web wallet uses it, and opens Lotus Qt and lotusd wallet files too. One setting lets an operator turn it off for every visitor.
items.alt: The browser node panel: tip, headers checked, peers
items.means: Your browser checks the chain itself instead of trusting one server.

items.text: One app to mine with your GPU, hold a wallet and vote with RANK on X (Linux for now). It is also a small peer of the network that checks block headers itself. Your keys stay on your computer: write down the recovery words or save a backup file before you put coins in.
items.alt: Lotus Desktop: create a wallet or bring yours
items.means: Mine and keep what you earn in one app, with keys on your own computer.

title: Live sync heights of peers

alerts.text: **Napoleon, 2026-12-21 20:50 UTC:** every node must run 12.5.1 or later before then. This version qualifies. Earlier versions, 12.4.x included, do not follow the chain after the fork.

items.text: Nodes tell their peers their height each time it moves, so the peer list shows how far a syncing node has got, updated every few seconds, instead of the height it had when it connected. For older peers the height is taken from the blocks they ask for.
A peer that is busy syncing and slow to answer pings is no longer disconnected while it keeps talking to the node.

title: Lighter thin nodes, a faster web UI, per-chain charts

alerts.text: **Napoleon, 2026-12-21 20:50 UTC:** every node must run 12.5.1 or later before then. This version qualifies. Earlier versions, 12.4.x included, do not follow the chain after the fork.

items.lead: Thin nodes stop rewriting their disk.
items.text: A thin node started from a snapshot no longer downloads old blocks again and again; its disk writes drop to what each new block needs.
items.alt: Thin nodes stop rewriting their disk

items.lead: Explorer: the first block is always indexed.
items.text: The explorer tables no longer depend on start-up timing for the genesis block.
items.alt: Explorer: the first block is always indexed

items.lead: A responsive web UI under load.
items.text: Idle browser and proxy connections no longer hold the node's request threads, so pages and the API answer at once while several tabs or a reverse proxy are connected.
items.alt: A responsive web UI under load

items.text: The difficulty and hashrate charts draw one series per chain (Lotus, Bitcoin, eCash, Bitcoin Cash, Litecoin), each in its own colour.
A peer's country now comes from exact address ranges, for IPv4 and IPv6, with its network operator. The table is built into the node: no address leaves it.

items.lead: Pages for tokens, blobs and games.
items.text: Tokens, blobs, POKR and eMPP get their own pages, and a protocol transaction shows its payload decoded field by field.
items.alt: Pages for tokens, blobs and games

title: Ready for the Napoleon fork

alerts.text: **Napoleon, 2026-12-21 20:50 UTC:** every node must run 12.5.1 or later before then. This version qualifies. Until Napoleon it follows the same rules as 12.4.x, so you can upgrade now. Earlier versions, 12.4.x included, do not follow the chain after the fork.

items.lead: Merged mining on real parent chains.
items.text: From Napoleon, merged-mined blocks must be anchored to real Bitcoin, eCash, Bitcoin Cash or Litecoin blocks.
items.alt: Merged mining on real parent chains

items.text: Litecoin pools that already merge-mine Lotus with standard AuxPoW need no change. SHA-256d pools (eCash, Bitcoin, Bitcoin Cash) name their chain in one place: `createauxblock <address> xec|btc|bch`, or `-auxpowalgo=<chain>` on the Lotus node.

items.lead: One difficulty lane per parent chain.
items.text: From Napoleon, merged mining on Bitcoin, eCash, Bitcoin Cash and Litecoin each has its own difficulty, and a miner picks the chain by its stratum port. Merged mining cannot crowd out native mining.
items.alt: One difficulty lane per parent chain

items.text: The explorer and the network pages show the parent chains Lotus follows.
From Napoleon, block rewards and pool payouts can be spent after 20 blocks (about 40 minutes).
The node tells you when a newer version is announced by enough of its peers.

title: Pool links that no longer stall, faster block connection, Taproot addresses, one GPU miner
consensus: none. The rules and the activation time are those of 12.4.13

alerts.text: **Napoleon, 2026-12-21 20:50 UTC:** every node must run 12.4.13 or later by then. This version qualifies.

**GPU miner users:** the `lotus-gpu-miner-amd` image and the `-nvidia` / `-amd` archives are no longer produced. Use `lotus-gpu-miner` for both vendors, and pass your own payout address: there is no built-in one any more. AMD cards were not tested on real hardware for this release.

items.text: Two pool nodes that connect no longer stop reading each other while both send their catch-up; such links used to stay dead until the ping timeout.
The explorer and module databases are written after the block, in order, on their own thread: connecting a large block takes about half the time. `-asyncindex=0` keeps the old path.
`sendrawtransactions` admits up to 1,000 transactions per call, 2.2 to 2.7 times faster than separate calls; `getblocktemplatelight` answers in under a millisecond.
The node wallet, the web wallet, the miners and the pool can create, receive on and spend from Taproot (`lotus_J…`) addresses. Legacy addresses stay the default.
A single program and image for NVIDIA and AMD, with `--backend auto|nvidia|amd`.

title: Faster relay, faster reads, and the wallet fix
consensus: none. The rules and the activation time are those of 12.4.13

alerts.text: **Napoleon, 2026-12-21 20:50 UTC:** every node must run 12.4.13 or later by then. This version qualifies.

items.text: `createwallet` and `loadwallet` work again on the release binaries. They failed for SQLite wallets in 12.4.13 and 12.4.14.
Between trusted nodes a burst of 500 transactions crosses each hop in 0.1 to 0.2 s instead of about 2 s, and a burst of 5,000 always arrives between ordinary peers.
`getblockchaininfo`, `getmempoolinfo` and the chain and mempool summaries no longer wait for the node's main locks; the one-second outliers under load are gone.
A thin node no longer floods its proof servers when a block has many inputs it does not hold. Upgrade proof servers to 12.4.15 first.
Less CPU spent on pool messages, with no change to the ledger.
A refreshed look for the node's dashboard.

title: Thin mode, explorer paging, safer RPC behind a proxy
consensus: none. The rules and the activation time are those of 12.4.13

alerts.text: **Napoleon, 2026-12-21 20:50 UTC:** every node must run 12.4.13 or later by then. This version qualifies.
**Known issue, fixed in 12.4.15:** these binaries cannot create or load an SQLite wallet, and a node started with `-wallet=` on such a wallet does not start. If you use the wallet, install 12.4.15.

items.text: `-thin=1` runs a node without the history: it proves the coins it needs from peers and checks them against the header chain. `-thin=utxo` starts from a UTXO snapshot.
Full nodes write a snapshot every 100 blocks, once its commitment is buried in the chain, and serve the newest one for download.
Address history with cursor paging, and batch endpoints for transactions and addresses.
JSON-RPC and the operator routes refuse a request that arrives through a reverse proxy, unless you set `-rpcallowforwarded=1`.
A second polish pass of the node's web interface.

title: The Napoleon network upgrade: required before 21 December 2026
consensus: yes. New rules activate at Napoleon, when the median time past of the previous block reaches 1797886200 (2026-12-21 20:50 UTC)

alerts.text:
**Every node operator, pool and exchange must run 12.4.13 or later before 2026-12-21 20:50 UTC.**
A node on an older version, or on any LotusiaStewardship release, leaves the chain at the first block that uses the new rules. There is no grace period.
Miners and pools that build their own coinbase must add the UTXO set commitment before that date.
**Known issue, fixed in 12.4.15:** these binaries cannot create or load an SQLite wallet, and a node started with `-wallet=` on such a wallet does not start. If you use the wallet, install 12.4.15.

items.text: From Napoleon a Lotus block can be mined together with Bitcoin or Litecoin: one parent header proves one Lotus block.
New script opcodes for contracts (introspection, `OP_MUL`, `OP_MULDIV`, Taproot state, `OP_CHECKBLOCKHASHVERIFY`) activate at Napoleon.
From Napoleon every block commits to the UTXO set in its coinbase, so a snapshot can be checked against the chain.
A node can start from a UTXO snapshot and validate the history in the background. Full nodes write one every 100 blocks.
